claims.text: Nanoscale confinement limits cooperative phase behavior in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons.
Increased thermal boundary resistance suppresses the continuous magnetostructural transition in low-dimensional FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Bulk FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys exhibit a continuous magnetostructural transition.
A brief post-deposition anneal improves grain connectivity in nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type samples.
A brief post-deposition anneal reduces local structural disorder in nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type samples.
Improved grain connectivity and reduced disorder partially restore cooperative magnetostructural behavior.
Annealing will increase the magnetocaloric effect relative to the as-deposited state during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Annealing will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the as-deposited state during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Finite-size effects in nanoscale geometry increase thermal boundary resistance.
Finite-size effects disrupt long-range magnetic interactions.
Increased thermal boundary resistance and disrupted long-range magnetic interactions produce a more distributed or stepwise, hysteretic phase transition.
Enhanced grain connectivity and reduced defect density produce a more coherent, bulk-like magnetostructural transition.
Annealing conditions can be selected that relieve nanoscale disorder without causing substantial phase segregation or undesired crystallographic changes.
Heat-transfer rate limits the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency under the proposed operating conditions.
